territorial_scope.description: Applies to digital labour platforms organising platform work performed in the Union, irrespective of their place of establishment; the directive is addressed to Member States.

evidence.quote: This Directive applies to digital labour platforms organising platform work performed in the Union, irrespective of their place of establishment or of the law otherwise applicable.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Sets EU minimum rules for digital labour platforms organising platform work in the Union: a rebuttable presumption of employment, limits and transparency duties for algorithmic management, and work declarations to authorities. Member States must transpose by 2 December 2026.
summary.long: Sets minimum rules for digital labour platforms organising platform work in the Union, wherever established. Art. 5 creates a rebuttable presumption of employment where facts indicating direction and control are found, for administrative and judicial proceedings other than tax, criminal or social security; Art. 4 requires procedures to determine correct employment status; Art. 3 extends protection to workers engaged through intermediaries. Chapter III governs algorithmic management: Art. 7 bans processing of listed personal data (e.g. emotional state, private conversations, biometric identification); Art. 8 requires a data-protection impact assessment; Art. 9 imposes information duties; Art. 10 requires human oversight and impact evaluation at least every two years, and human decisions on account restriction or termination; Art. 11 grants explanation, human contact, written reasons and review. Arts. 12-14 cover safety and health risk evaluation and consultation. Art. 16 requires declaration of platform work to authorities; Art. 17 information updated every six months. Arts. 18-23 provide redress, representative actions, evidence disclosure and protection from adverse treatment. Art. 24 applies GDPR supervision and fine ceilings to Arts. 7-11 and requires effective, dissuasive, proportionate penalties. Transposition is due by 2 December 2026.

‘digital labour platform’ means a natural or legal person providing a service which meets all of the following requirements:

The definition of ‘digital labour platform’ laid down in point (a) of paragraph 1 does not include providers of a service whose primary purpose is to exploit or share assets or by means of which individuals who are not professionals can resell goods.
‘platform work’ means work organised through a digital labour platform and performed in the Union by an individual on the basis of a contractual relationship

‘person performing platform work’ means an individual performing platform work, irrespective of the nature of the contractual relationship or the designation of that relationship by the parties involved;
‘platform worker’ means any person performing platform work who has or is deemed to have an employment contract or an employment relationship
‘intermediary’ means a natural or legal person that, for the purpose of making platform work available to or through a digital labour platform:

‘workers’ representatives’ means representatives of platform workers, such as trade unions and representatives who are freely elected by the platform workers in accordance with national law and practice;
